title: Keep originals and version your drafts

questions.prompt: Why keep your original before AI editing?

choices.text: Because the original will always be better than every edited version without exception
Because tools require you to keep it
To see what changed and go back if needed

questions.correct_answer: To see what changed and go back if needed
questions.intro: When you edit with AI help, KEEP YOUR ORIGINAL. A tool may rewrite more than you asked, and without the original you cannot see what changed or go back. VERSION your drafts: save copies with clear names such as "essay_v1_mine," "essay_v2_ai_edit," "essay_v3_final," or use your app's version history. Before accepting a big change, compare it with the previous version. Versioning also helps with honesty and grading: you can show how your work developed. A good rule is "never overwrite your only copy."

sections.skill: Compare versions with photos of a room before you redecorate

questions.prompt: Why take a photo before redecorating?

choices.text: Because photos of rooms are needed to buy new paint at any hardware store
To put things back if you dislike the change

questions.correct_answer: To put things back if you dislike the change
questions.intro: Before you repaint and rearrange a room, you take a PHOTO. If you hate the new look, the photo shows exactly where everything was so you can put it back. If you take a photo after each step, you can see which change made it better or worse. Saving versions of a document works the same way: each saved copy is a "photo" of your work at that moment.

questions.prompt: A photo after each step is like what?

choices.text: Saving a version after each edit
Deleting the old version each time a change is made so only the newest remains

questions.correct_answer: Saving a version after each edit

questions.prompt: A folder has "final," "final2" and "really_final." What is the problem?

choices.text: Nothing, because the most recent file is always the one with the longest file name
It is unclear which is which

questions.correct_answer: It is unclear which is which
questions.intro: Versioning only helps if names and dates are clear. "final," "final2" and "really_final" become confusing; dates and short descriptions work better ("2026-03-14_after_peer_review"). Keep track of which version you actually submitted or sent. When several people edit, agree on one master copy so changes do not get lost. And remember that copying text into a chat does not save a version for you; save your own file.
